macro.regime: Hawkish Fed repricing collides with live Mideast war-risk premium
macro.narrative: Markets repriced hawkish-Fed and Mideast-war risk simultaneously on Tue Sep 1: the S&P 500 fell 0.71% to 7631.47 (Nasdaq -1.03%, Russell 2000 -1.23%) as VIX spiked 9.5% to 16.34, while WTI surged 5.81% to $90.74 after fresh Iranian-linked attacks on a Saudi and a South Korean tanker in the Strait of Hormuz drew US CENTCOM strikes on IRGC targets along Iran's southern coast (Bandar Abbas, Jask, Chabahar and others) -- a distinct second escalation beyond Sunday's Jordan/UAE strikes. Gold and silver sold off hard (GLD -2.86%, SLV -3.68%, GDX -3.90%, SILJ -4.18%) as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole stance kept pushing September rate-hike odds toward 57-72% (from ~35% pre-Jackson Hole), with dollar strength and 10y yields near 4.81% (highest since Jan 2025) overwhelming the usual safe-haven bid. Underneath the inflation-focused hawkishness (ISM Prices Paid stuck at 71.1%, CPI 3.4% y/y July), labor data is quietly softening -- ISM Manufacturing decelerated to 54.6 from 55.6 and JOLTS missed at 7.271M with June revised down to 7.182M -- setting up today's ADP and Friday's NFP (cons 55K vs -23K prior) as the pivotal swing factor for the Sep 16 FOMC. Credit markets remain a conspicuous holdout of calm (IG 78bp, HY 260bp, HY tightened 19bp in August) even as equities/vol/gold price in more caution, while China's calibrated (not broad) easing stance after a second straight PMI contraction (49.8) adds a further mixed cross-current. Breadth confirms the deterioration is real and broad, not just index-level: NYSE decliners led 2.32:1 (Nasdaq 2.76:1), 52-week new lows overtook highs (45 highs vs 68 lows, a -23 spread flipping from +110 on 28 Aug), the McClellan Oscillator fell to -231.30, and the S&P's % of members above their 200-day/50-day MAs dropped to 62.62%/45.52% from 68.78%/52.88% four sessions earlier.
